summary: Our group developed a software that describes how the spinal column moves under certain circumstances, such as microgravity and muscular tension. We thought of this solution because our spine is one of the most, if not the most, important structure of the body since it protects most of the central nervous system. It addresses the challenge by making sure that astronauts don't need to check their spinal health themselves.
details:
S.P.I.N.A. is currently a demonstration prototype of a real-world product designed to be powered by external and spinal body scanners.

Built using HTML5 Canvas, CSS3, JavaScript, the prototype features a 26-vertebra physics engine to simulate microgravity biomechanics. By integrating external scan data, the final product will map each astronaut's exact anatomy, blending human-centric design with accessibility to deliver tailored decompression routines and protect long-term spinal health in space.
